newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Ratsiraka, Zafy race close in Madagascar elections.
newsitem.headline: Ratsiraka, Zafy race close in Madagascar elections.

text.p: Former Madagascar Marxist military ruler Didier Ratsiraka was still in the lead over ex-president Albert Zafy in returns in a run-off presidential poll on Monday but the race was closer than earlier forecast.

Zafy, trailing heavily after initial results from the Sunday run-off elections, put up a strong showing as results came in from rural districts on Monday and even managed a healthier-than-forecast showing in the capital Antananarivo.
According to provisional results, Ratsiraka had 51.75 percent of the votes whereas ex-president Zafy, a surgery professor, had a close 48.25 percent of the ballot.

In Antananarivo, where results were almost complete, Ratsiraka had 52.71 percent of the vote compared to Zafy's 47.29 percent. In the first round, Zafy had managed only 4.0 percent of the capital's vote compared to Ratsiraka's 38 percent.
Earlier results in Antananarivo had been closer, with Zafy taking 41,774 of the votes against Ratsiraka's 41,852.
The interior ministry put voter turnout at 50.71 percent.

Election observers said that with an average participation rate of 50 percent and if current trends did not change, a new president would be elected by just 25 percent of the 6.5 million registered voters in the Indian Ocean island.
Political observers who had previously forecast an easy Ratsiraka victory were changing their minds as result came out.
Results coming from the rural polling stations showed a strong showing for Zafy, making the race very close.
An opinion poll taken shortly before Sunday's run-off showed Ratsiraka with 60 percent to 40 percent for Zafy.
Political analysts were predicting that Ratsiraka, a 60-year-old retired admiral, would carry four of Madagascar's six provinces.
The two where Zafy was believed stronger were Antsiranana in northern Madagascar and Toliara in the south, both of which are less populous compared to the rest of the island, analysts said.
Zafy led in the extreme northern Ansiranana area whereas Ratsiraka was ahead in his birthplace of Tomasina in northeast.

In the central region, Ratsiraka had 53.77 percent of vote against Zafy's 46.24 percent whereas in Mahanjaga, a port in the northwest, Zafy took 51.75 percent versus with Ratsiraka's 48.25 percent with votes counted from 34 of 51 polling stations.

The vote in the Indian Ocean island republic was called after Zafy, 69, elected to succeed Ratsiraka in 1993, was impeached by parliament in July for abuse of his authority and exceeding his constitutional powers.
Zafy had earlier won a referendum empowering him, rather than parliament, to appoint the prime minister.
Ratsiraka returned from 19 months of voluntary exile in France at the end of September, after a campaign that aroused little excitement.
None of the 15 candidates in the first round in November won the necessary 50 per cent of votes to secure outright victory.
Ratsiraka led the first-round poll with 36.6 per cent of the vote, against 23.4 per cent for Zafy.
In a radio interview on Sunday Ratsiraka said he was confident of victory but would support Zafy if he lost.
Final results are expected in about a week.
